name: Reserve Bank of India
stance_note: No general practice of publishing comments received on discussion papers. Commenters self-publish instead (NASSCOM posted its own submission on the Charges paper; Vidhi posted its 2019 PA/PG submission). Individual comment-archives exist only because commenters chose to publish. RTI is the fallback route.

name: Securities and Exchange Board of India
stance_note: Posts consultation papers and the comments received on its public-comments portal; a board-approved procedure (18 Dec 2024) formalised pre-legislative consultation for regulation-making.

name: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
stance_note: Consultation papers published on its portal. In June 2026 IRDAI proposed a formal regulation-making framework: minimum 21-day public comment window and a general statement of response to comments published by the date regulations are notified. Until notified, publication of comments is not a settled practice.

name: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
stance_note: Runs a Public Comments section; its discussion papers instruct commenters to submit through the website with stakeholder categories, and comments are published there.

name: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
stance_note: Consultation papers published on the site (e.g. Sept 2025 valuation-alignment paper via PIB). Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking.

name: International Financial Services Centres Authority
stance_note: Consultation papers listed on ifsca.gov.in. Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking.
